title: Climate and Energy Flow
seo_title: Climate Worksheets: Energy Budget, Milankovitch Cycles and Ice Cores (Earth Science)
standard_text: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems result in changes in climate.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on climate and energy flow (NGSS HS-ESS2-4): Earth's energy budget, warming and cooling causes, time scales and ice-core data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy in vs. energy out sets climate.
key_sub: Greenhouse gases, the Sun, orbits, volcanoes and ice all change the energy balance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Climate changes when the flow of energy in and out of Earth changes.

  • Absorbed sunlight = incoming − reflected. If more energy comes in than goes out, Earth warms.
  • Warming: more greenhouse gases, less ice. Cooling: volcanic particles, less sunlight, more snow and ice.
  • Causes act on different time scales: eruptions (years), solar and ocean cycles (years to decades), orbit changes (tens of thousands of years), moving continents (millions).
Example

340 W/m² in, 100 reflected. Absorbed?

340 − 100

Answer: 240 W/m²

Example

A big eruption adds sulfur particles. Effect?

Reflects sunlight

Answer: cooling for 1–3 years

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up weather and climate.
  • Thinking greenhouse gases block incoming sunlight.
  • Thinking one cause explains every climate change.

Mainly slow changes in Earth's orbit and tilt (Milankovitch cycles), amplified by feedbacks from ice and greenhouse gases.

faq.q: How are weather and climate different?
faq.a: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere; climate is the average pattern over 30 years or more.

items.q: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth?
c: They absorb infrared energy given off by Earth and send some back down.

items.q: Less summer sunlight reaches high northern latitudes. Does this tend to warm or cool the climate?
c: it only changes weather for one day
items.e: More energy kept in → warming; less energy in or more reflected → cooling.

items.q: What sets Earth's climate in the long run?
c: the balance between energy coming in from the Sun and energy going out to space
